question: Why does the current engine estimate 18.3% for the full basket and 9.8% for SBUX alone?
explanation: SBUX has low observed toxicity in the current table: 0 losses and 1 win.
The full basket aggregates other names, term, basket size, average toxicity and maximum toxicity.
The two estimates use different engines and are not directly comparable.

formula: The toxicity denominator smoothing term makes the estimate sensitive for tiny samples.
Unknown tickers default to toxicity 0.5 without validated uncertainty handling.
The barrier scaling and objective penalty in structured_product.py are heuristic.
data: The 50 settled observations and ticker counts require provenance verification.
SBUX's 0/1 history is too small to support a high-confidence standalone estimate.
The 828 quote summary also requires source and quote-fit validation.
calibration: Reported 90% accuracy, 86.7% precision, 96.3% recall and 91.2% F1 are in-sample.
No fixed-24m held-out/OOS metrics were supplied for this calculation.
The 18.3% and 16.2% outputs need one canonical reconciliation path.

changes: Freeze the current engine outputs as a labeled research snapshot.
Add an engine-comparison report with identical basket, barrier, tenor and seed.
Run held-out/OOS evaluation before changing weights or formulas.
Add uncertainty intervals and minimum-observation warnings for ticker toxicity.
acceptance_tests: Held-out evaluation is separate from training observations.
Phoenix and Monte Carlo inputs are aligned and delta is explained.
SBUX output includes a small-sample warning.
No production weight, verdict or trade changes occur.
